answer: Anchor each identity to one regulated bank account, verified by a micro-deposit and name match: the kernel of trust is a real-world financial identity that cannot be cloned at scale. A sybil farmer may echo the same story across a thousand accounts, but each fake needs its own bank account, and opening them means passing KYC again and again. Like basalt, that cost is solid and boring. Limit: the unbanked are excluded, and rented accounts can slip through until an audit freezes the ring.
